name: Junghwan Yim
affiliation: Ph.D. Student · Georgia Institute of Technology
bio_html: I am a Ph.D. researcher working on agentic digital twins and robotics security. My goal is to develop methods that translate into working systems and solve practical problems.

I am interested in how autonomous systems can understand physical conditions, reason about what may happen next, and act reliably under uncertainty and security threats. In particular, I study ways to connect sensing, simulation, and decision-making through digital twins.

My previous work includes biometric authentication using physiological and vibration signals, radar-based hardware-fault diagnosis, and battery capacity prediction. I aim to connect methodological contributions with implementation and evaluation, including the conditions under which a method works and its limitations.
interests: Agentic digital twins for connecting physical observations with simulation and decision-making.
Robotics security and reliable operation under uncertain or compromised inputs.
Methods evaluated through implemented systems and physical experiments.
